5. This app is versatile. We enjoy the back dating feature.

reviews.title: best app
reviews.text:
After testing a long list of chore-tracking and household management apps with my wife, Tody is the one we finally stuck with and for good reason.

The cross-platform integration between iPhone, iPad, and Mac is absolutely seamless. Whether I update a chore on my Mac or my wife checks something off on her iPhone, the sync is instantaneous and flawless every single time. It just works beautifully.

The user interface is a breeze: clean, intuitive, and thoughtfully designed. There’s no clutter, no unnecessary animations, and absolutely no learning curve. Tody gives you exactly what you need, and nothing you don’t.

What truly sets it apart is how it motivates and empowers everyone in the household to take ownership of tasks without nagging or micromanaging. It turns mundane chores into a shared, trackable system  and actually reduces tension around housework. No more “I thought you were going to do that” arguments.

We’ve tried many apps before. All had some limitation or frustrating quirk. Tody is the first one that feels like it was made with real users in mind.

reviews.title: Great app so far!
reviews.text: Update: It seems as though the devs have taken my suggestion and implemented it in a way with personalized lists of tasks you select. I’m not a huge fan of the way they did it with a timer and pausing/resetting. Just a simple list would’ve been fine. But it functions the same way I suppose. Unfortunately, even though this app would now be a 5-star due to doing most all that I require…the app is often broken. I open it and sometimes only get a black screen. Not sure what the issue is all of a sudden, but now and then I have this issue. Eventually it works, but it is quite annoying. Original: I love that now my husband and I are keeping track our cleaning chores and when they need to be done. Used to be we wouldn’t clean unless something was really nasty and needed cleaned, which left our house always looking gross and our guests probably grossed out. Not anymore! Though there is about an hour’s-worth of initial setup required, the way the chores are structured, the entire house will eventually be cleaned, but since each piece is staggered, you won’t feel overwhelmed. Just a few chores one day, a few the next. I do have a few gripes/suggestions however. One is minor: there are chores such as “dust (quick)” and “dust (thorough)”. If you decide you want to do both, you had best add them to your list at the same time and stay on top of their due dates in order for them to be synchronized. I wish there was some way to have them synchronize automatically if they are both on the list. Because mine weren’t, I ended up deleting the quick because I kept having the thorough come up like 2 days later. My second suggestion is for there to be a way to assign tasks to participants on a one-off basis. Like I know you can simply assign people to always be in charge of certain things. However, if you were to load up the list of things that need to be done for that day, there doesn’t seem to be a way to say “you do this and I’ll do that,” then get those things in a personalized task list so each person can go through and check them off. What this leads to is, if you have a lot of chores to get done in a weekend, you’re constantly reloading the full list, conferring with others in the household as to which ones everyone will be doing, then loading the full list again to find the tasks you did and mark them as done. That is just not efficient. One more thing...it shouldn’t be so expensive for multiple people in the same household to download this app. Like if you have 2 adults and 3 children participating, that’s a sizable investment. I think it should be that the first person to download is full price, then each subsequent download to join another household will have some sort of discount, like half off. My 2 cents. Still a great app and money well-spent for a couple in a small house with no kids at home (we have to do ALL the chores!!!).

It also doesn’t overwhelm us with notifications so the days that we are able to clean, we just open up the app and can find a chore that we can do that day to mark as done! reviews.title: Great features, no subscription
reviews.text: I just realized this app has no reviews, and I felt the need to support it! This is a project management cleaning app for a household (or multiple households) that works on iPhones and Androids. I love that it has a one-time fee instead of a subscription model. It's easily customizable, and you can switch off tasks if you like. You can also pause various tasks or go on "vacation" mode. I also use it for yearly reminders that I don't want to forget (e.g. purge the supply closet). There are two features that would be cool to add: 1) some kind of seasonal mode because I'd like to do certain tasks more often in the summer vs the winter; and 2) a way to declare a task "still clean" and extend the deadline for it without checking it as complete and thus switching to another household member. Otherwise, SUCH a useful app.

Android I think is different. - Ease of use - the app is easy to see up your rooms/locations and the task associated, timeframes, and assignments to family members - you are ready to go - The administrator is in control of the app although you can mark off your tasks, once complete - Consistency - you don't have to think about what neds to be done because the app let's you know when you have tasks through notifications - Routines- No tasks is left undone, once complete base on the timeframe set, you are told when it needs to be done - Effort Levels - This is a great way to figure out what you may want to tackle first, perhaps the easy; to get them out of the way first or hard to just get them out the way - Family involvement - you can identify family members tasks and efforts and perhaps put a monetary value to their work to give an allowance or bonus Cons: - Sort Features - I would enhance that you could either sort or search for a particular feature such as dusting, vacuuming, etc so that if you want to do all at one time or get ahead of a task for another room, you can do so I will say that my husband is pleased with the consistency of the cleaning because I don't have view the space to see what gets done or think about the last time it was completed. For example, when was the last time I cleaned the outside my cabinets or sealed and polished the granite. This App is well worth the money and for someone who does not spend money on Apps (Except for Pandora). The BEST productivity app for your home.

reviews.title: Gamification done right
reviews.text:
I came here by way of a recommendation from an ADHD focused podcast. I’ve previously looked at and tried out a few other apps, but almost immediately found them clunky and time consuming to set up, then the app was quickly abandoned after a few days or weeks. (Because yes, we have ADHD…)

The preset rooms, suggested tasks for each room, and frequency suggestions is a SPECTACULAR out of the box feature. A few more for pets or more detailed cleaning could be useful, but this is truly a monumentally helpful app in the set up stages. Not having to painstakingly think, “well… how often DO I think I’ll need to clean the oven…?” when starting out is a massive relief. 

I also really like the visual queues — the splotches as well as green/yellow/red indicators to show dirtiness, and both can be configured or turned off in preferences. Dusty is an added bonus. He’s sort of cute but gross, and adds just a little extra motivation to compete against, which is especially helpful if you live alone or your housemates aren’t onboard with the app. 

I especially like the nuance of the color bars, that vary between “just cleaned” and “not quite due.” A lot of other apps, or hand written checklists, end up feeling like an item must either be “just cleaned” or “completely filthy.” For ADHDer’s like me, that can make it feel pointless to engage in the smaller daily tasks, when dirt isn’t visibly overwhelming —yet. “Why do the dishes if the sink isn’t overflowing?”

I hope I can come back and update my review in a couple of months, when I can better evaluate the long term staying power. But so far it’s great.

reviews.title: This App is Worth Every Penny
reviews.text:
I am a parent who works overnights and has ADHD— I have tried every cleaning app there is. I always inevitably become overwhelmed with constant reminders to do things, get behind, and then feel guilty. 

I have been using TODY for almost a year now and it is a game changer. This is my first ever review of any app, but I can’t resist. Here are just a few of the things that I LOVE about it:
-I don’t get alarms every day telling me I need to do this or that. I open the app, check the progress bars, and get whatever checked off that I need to 
-I don’t need to keep track of what needs to be cleaned in my head OR wait until it looks dirty. It is external executive functioning. 
-my partner and I both use it. Gone are the days of either of us nagging or feeling overwhelmed by mess. If things begin to get messy, we can both see that, and independently begin to clean. We NEVER have conflict or frustrating over cleaning tasks anymore. 
-depressed? Sick? Can’t get stuff done for a week? That’s okay! The app is still there for you when you are mentally and physically able to clean. It accounts for not being 100% all of the time. You don’t get shamed or need to feel guilty. 
-positive messages. Getting stuff done is rewarding. My seven-year-old LOVES to help clean around the house to see what message it tells him. It is also so satisfying seeing a bar turn from red to green. 
-it is easy for me to pick “I want to do __ tody tasks today” instead of thinking “I have to deep clean the entire kitchen today”. It makes cleaning manageable. 
-things that I NEVER think of— for example, cleaning the curtains once a year, don’t get neglected. 

I couldn’t say enough positives about this app. I have highly recommended it to my friends and family, and would highly recommend it to anyone debating purchasing it.

I love the status bars for tasks, grouping by areas, ability to customize completion frequency. The only major drawback for me is the lack of notifications for individual tasks. For someone with ADHD like me, seeing a notification like “you have 7 tasks due today” is just so discouraging. I end up never opening the app to look at specific tasks that are due because it’s an extra step and I already start feeling like there are several things I need to get done. Tasks pile up, I see a red bar, I stress out, eventually stop using the app all together… It would be so helpful to have an option to turn on (or off) notifications for each task individually, what time of the day I want to receive it (e.g., do the dishes at 7pm, wipe the stove at 8am), and whether I want it on the day it’s due and/or maybe a few days before. That way I’d know when I need to get things done without feeling overwhelmed. For other tasks that take longer periods of time to become relevant again, I can open the app and actually see the status bar when I check off things I got done because of individual notifications. Otherwise, excellent app and I’ll keep making attempts at making it work for me!

Haha!  2. It has helped me to only focus on what’s right in front of me. In the past I’d look at all the things not getting done and berate myself about them but those days are gone because I know that messy room or that cluttered closet will have its designated time, and if that time isn’t today, I can let it go!  3. I just love having everything in the same place. I put my freelance work, bills, garden tasks, daily Bible reading, cooking, hobbies, random reminders like signing kids up for swimming lessons, even taking showers (yes, apparently I need an app for that, haha), in this app. I love that it helps me prioritize all types of things - not just cleaning! reviews.title: Best app ever
reviews.text:
Having suffered from depression for many years, I have struggled with maintaining everyday routines. I set up this app for my household chores, as it is intended, and took awhile to get using it.  But, once I did, it made a huge difference. If I’m behind on one thing or another, I feel so much less stress, because I can easily see what to prioritize and be more productive overall. Within a week of using this daily, I noticed that my mind was clear of the chores I needed to do, even if I was still behind, because I knew if I kept working, I would get to them eventually. The system is so beautiful, that it made a psychological impact on my life. 

Many reviewers have mentioned that they use this app for other life lists, but I’ve had bad luck in the past combining too many things into one place. I wrote the developers with a suggestion to create another app that uses this concept for work / life / self care balance, and they kindly responded. So, not only is the app great, but clearly the creators are as well.

Rather than setting a rigid schedule (you can still do it that way if you prefer) your task schedule has a bit more wiggle room by showing you how badly a task needs doing. The only thing that isn’t working well for me is “anytime” tasks. They don’t seem to show up in any of the todo lists, and it would be nice if there were a section for “anytime” tasks in the daily todo list. Otherwise it’s out of sight out of mind! Overall the app has been a huge help in sharing housework assignments and keeping things from getting too far gone. No more marathon cleaning for me!

I like the fact I can determine how often things need cleaned and it simply keeps track. My anxiety on what needs cleaned is now under control. It’s awesome how each task is green to red. reviews.title: Decent idea, but way overpriced for what it's worth

The app alsr has quite a few frustrating moments - for the $16 we paid for 2 apps (for me and my wife) I expected user experience to be MUCH more smooth. 

Cons:
- Family sync doesn't work or is unreliable, but they charge for every user. My wife has an outdated version of our task list and isn't getting updates for tasks marked done on my phone - and there's no "force sync" button. We have to use only one phone to track our chores because of that. Kinda defeats the purpose, and money on one of the apps is wasted.
-App often doesn't close properly. If I open the app, use it and then do something else - when I go back to Tody, it shows "loading" screen forever. Have to close and reopen. Not unbearable but very annoying.
- "Support" feature in the app doesn't work. Just fails with "check your mail configuration".

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.text: You definitely need to learn how to use this. The key to cleaning is to PICK UP STUFF! I have been working with a professional organizer and the place to start is at the front door. Whenever anyone comes over, you want to first clean what they will see. Then work on your bedroom. This sets the tone. I also do dishes and trash daily and laundry on a slow day at home - Sundays. My personal organizer calls it the “illusion of cleanliness” and her name is Marie Ricks. She has written many books on cleaning and organization! I’ve used Tody in the past and love it, but it becomes SO BURDENSOME depending on how it is used. I group cleaning into an “area” called “cleaning reboot” for surface cleaning, vacuuming, kitchen/bath, etc. I love that I can assign this to professional cleaners and other family members. I also have an area for “morning routine” “daily clean” “tasks” and “evening routine”. I skip tasks I don’t want to do that day by pausing them. The order of the areas I work through somewhat chronologically. SET TO RELAXED! It is still sparkling. Key is that many presets are missing TIDY! Do TIDY tasks every day and surface cleaning as far out as you can handle. This gives the illusion of cleanliness! Don’t just trust me. Trust a professional organizer. Marie is the best!

reviews.title: The App That Just Keeps Getting Better
reviews.text:
Tody is a game changer. I tried several different techniques to try to manage keeping my home clean, and I’d give up on all of them. Tody is an app I’ve stuck with for over six months now. 

What makes Tody different? Tody doesn’t demand a part of your day in cleaning. Rather, it recommends to you when you should clean something. What do I mean by that? Some cleaning systems want you to zone clean, so for example, Kitchen on Mondays, Bathrooms on Tuesdays, and so on. That’s great until you sat in the ER with your kid all Monday evening, or any other convenient excuse. Now you start getting backlogged and start feeling like you’re failing. 

With Tody, you’re given a heads up a task is due. Don’t have time today? It’ll stay on your list until you get to it, and then reset the clock from there. Realize that vacuuming the spare bedroom that never gets used every week is a waste of time? Change the frequency to every two weeks, or every month. Toilet needs cleaned more than once a week because you have a household full of teenage boys? Change the frequency, AND assign the task to them until they learn how to aim better. 

Also, for those trying to build habits because you’ve never kept a house clean successfully before, Tody keeps track of how many tasks you do. So, if you want to treat yourself to a pizza because you’ve gotten all the tasks done in a week, or buy yourself a TV soundbar because you completed 500 points worth of tasks in a month and you’re proud of the housekeeper you’ve become, this is your faithful scorekeeper. 

There are dozens of techniques for habit building out there. I can’t promise this is the method that will work for you, but it is a well thought out and maintained app, and it’s worth a try!

TL;DR: This app is chock full of features, and worth it. Give it a try!

reviews.title: Brilliant concept, UX could be better
reviews.text:
The overall concept is brilliant and is a game changer for thinking differently/approaching household tasks. Rather than chunk out by room or just spending more time less frequently cleaning, this app nudges you to clean more frequently, doing a few small tasks per day. So you gradually clean over the course of a week. Kind of revolutionary and I’m noticing it feels less daunting to clean, since you’re doing it all more gradually and actually staying more on top of it. 

With a general redesign visually and some
UX improvements, this app would be incredible: 

- hide completed tasks
- allow swipe gestures to actually clear/archive a task in one gesture rather than two
- allow undue after completing a task
- task status page is confusing (pause, skip back, forward?) 
- notifications with actual items or integrate with calendar would be massively helpful
- the general clunkiness of the overall design and UX (feels like a Microsoft product from the early 00s)

reviews.title: Can’t manually order tasks.
reviews.text:
I do really like this app. It helps me keep track of what needs to be done and prevents me from over-cleaning when something doesn’t need to be done yet.  The features are simple and not overdone and it is intuitive to use.

However, it is lacking one specific ability. While I can manually order the areas, I cannot manually order tasks within an area.  When cleaning, tasks need to be completed in a certain order. For example, one always dusts the tops of cabinets first and vacuums last. This way one is not re-vacuuming cabinet dust that may fall on the floor after the floor has already been vacuumed. This app determines it’s own order of tasks and it is not in a good order.  I have to try to hunt through the list of tasks to figure out what to do next and inevitably miss a task. I end up dusting the tops of cabinets after I have vacuumed and have to re-vacuum. I spend as much time managing the app as I do cleaning and find myself just not using the app because of this.

I really want to use this app on a daily basis so I really, really hope the developers are able to make the task list be ordered manually .

reviews.title: Great Household Organizational Tool
reviews.text: This tool allows you to set a frequency for each household task. Tasks are organized by room, and there are also options for the whole house, garage, and outdoors tasks. Initially, you choose one of three levels for how clean you want to keep things. This sets a default frequency for each task to get you started. Then, you go through and adjust the tasks, areas, and frequencies to your liking. The app creates a cleaning list and shows tasks with color coding to represent how urgent/ close to due the tasks are- green for not due for awhile, red for overdue, etc. There is a pause button for seasonal tasks. For example, packing school bags can be paused for the summer and weeding the garden can be paused for the winter. It is also possible to schedule infrequent tasks that happen every few months or even yearly. The thing that makes this better than a typical cleaning checklist or schedule is that items can easily be scheduled for unusual frequencies. Maybe every week is too often to clean the shower, but two weeks is too infrequent. It is easy to set the frequency to 10 days because the app will keep track for you, optimizing your use of time. And if you don’t get to it, the app will keep rolling it over to the next day for you. If you decide to do it a couple days early, the app will adjust for that, too. This is one of the most helpful apps that I use day-to-day. I highly recommend it.

Normally I would never pay for an app, but this looked like it might be exactly what I was looking for. It is wonderful. My mind has been freed of the constant thinking about chores. 

I use this in conjunction with the Flylady concept and they work perfectly together. My only question is when will it be available for non-apple products? My Samsung phone for instance.

Thank you for developing this!

reviews.title: Game changer
reviews.text: I am a big time procrastinator and “ I’ve gotta clean......(kitchen, bathroom, car etc) was always in my head but seemed so time consuming I pushed it to another day. This app breaks things up into small tasks. Most take 5 minutes! So while cleaning my entire bathroom sounded awful, I can take a few minutes to wipe down the sink and mirror- DONE! Checking off the task is so gratifying! These little tasks add up and my house is CLEAN- probably for the first time in my life. I know.... not rocket science but for someone who put off housework this is a game changer. I can’t wait to show my college age kids because they have roommates and sharing the app and chores looks awesome and can probably save some roommate arguments. But I bet they’ll be thankful I didn’t have this when they lived at home!! Haha! This would be so great to keep track of family household chores without the nagging- well, less nagging! 😊

reviews.title: Beat app for housekeeping!
reviews.text: Helps my ADD self stay focused with no time for thinking and rethinking before I get started!

reviews.title: Changed my life
reviews.text: I used to literally have panic attacks, feeling overwhelmed by housework to do lists. Tody helps me break things down into scheduled tasks that I can handle without stress. Plus, it reminds me to clean areas I haven’t even thought about cleaning. I love it.

reviews.title: Killer App - Missing stronger notifications
reviews.text: This App is easily 5 stars if the notification capabilities were expanded.  Example would be to follow someone and receive notifications on what they did, added or moved.  Also daily digests with details would be great.  Also has no widget available.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: Easy to use. Exactly what I was looking for.

reviews.title: Best cleaning app
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for almost two years and it’s the only thing that’s helped me stay organized enough to keep my house clean. I love it and I recommend it to everyone who asks me how I keep my house clean and organized as a mother of four small children.

reviews.title: Good but could be great!
reviews.text:
I have mental disorders that make it difficult to stay on task and remember things. It’s also hard to prioritize things the way I should. This app helps a great deal with remembering to clean things I’d usually forget, but I feel like it could be so much better... especially for the price I paid ($7.99 at the time.) I don’t feel like the app is worth the price. A price maybe, just not that price. 

I have a reoccurring issue where I cannot copy rooms. Every time I try to copy a room, the app crashes. When I reopen it, the room will be copied but none of the tasks are in the new room. 

As a single parent- there are tons of (free) apps that are more helpful because they cater more toward kids. They’re more appealing to their eye. The avatars are helpful but they’re far too simplistic and low quality to appeal to kids. For example, looking at the app called “OurHome” it offers a more appealing look, and an integrated reward program. I see that this company is attempting to break this app design down into multiple apps, such as the life app you offer that’s essentially the same as this one. It costs $5 less but you could do the same thing with this app by using different labels. That gives me a negative impression of the company. I realize you’re here to make money but word of mouth being your most valuable advertisement, it’s more beneficial to offer all these features in one app. I say this because if you go create a separate app for kids, it’ll just make it worse. I don’t want to have multiple apps to manage my day, I want 1 app to do everything. I think everyone feels that way for the most part. If I were in the position to create an app like this, I would use tody as it is, as a base plan but create a main menu. The cleaning as it is now, under the cleaning menu. The life goals in a separate menu, and adding in the kids section would be a major plus. 
Most people looking for an app to organize their day, have kids. 
My kids all have iPhones. But they hate this app. So even though it’s cool that I can set the app to alert them of their own chore list, if I can’t get them to use it it’s pointless.

reviews.title: Love it! It inspires me to get stuff done!
reviews.text: I have tried other routine reminder type apps, and some are pretty good. However I usually stop using them fairly quickly. Tody feels very different in a good way. It is user friendly, adaptable, ( a big plus!) and I love the way it makes me anticipate my To Do items in such a way that I want to be proactive. Highly recommended! Thanks for this simple to use and supremely useful application.

reviews.title: Doesn’t Sync
reviews.text: This app was super cool when it worked. It no longer syncs between our phones, so it defeats the purpose of sharing our tasks. We have tried troubleshooting and nothing has worked. It’s kind of discouraging because I never pay for apps, but decided to try out this paid app. The App Store says I can’t get a refund because I purchased more than 90 days ago.

reviews.title: Get it!!
reviews.text:
This app is the BEST!  If I had a dollar for every time I recommended it to friends..... there should be a referral program!  
We ‘fired’ the cleaning lady in exchange for this app. It helps me delegate chores to my four kids and keeps me cleaning the things that often go unnoticed. I even use it to remind me to change furnace filters and do car maintenance.  Totally customizable and fabulous!

reviews.title: I don’t write reviews but...
reviews.text: I FREAKING LOVE THIS APP! It has seriously made my family so much cleaner, more organized, and happier. I used to get overwhelmed by a dirty house now I know just what I need to do next.

reviews.title: Best chore app
reviews.text: I tried four free apps before trying this one- and none compare. Super easy to use and set up. Totally worth it!

reviews.title: Crashes
reviews.text: After most recent update, app crashes constantly. Useless until this problem is fixed.

reviews.title: Exactly what I needed.
reviews.text: So worth it. Suggests items and length of time for each room and has a custom option. Use it everyday. Keeps me on track and house clean!

reviews.title: Needs a few enhancements
reviews.text: How to delete a chore? How to delete an area? How to reorder? Help!

reviews.title: Godsend for screen addicted kids
reviews.text:
My son loves this! He wants to collect all the tasks he can and this takes the guess work out of what needs to be done and when. 

I am very pleased with this app - the lacking star is because I’d really love to be able to assign chores to a specific day instead of, in the beginning, it gauged timeframes by s/m/l type completion ratios. After the first time doing each task, it’ll start the REAL countdown. It’s not so helpful for reminding me of filter changes, vent cleaning, etc the first time around. I’ll settle in in a few months or so.

Great idea!
